title: Detection Validation and Decay
content_md: Detection validation is the practice of proving a detection rule still fires on the events it was written to catch. Detection decay is the silent failure of a rule that once worked, after a log source, schema, or parser changes underneath it. A rule that is deployed and enabled is not a rule that is proven to work. How do you know a detection rule still works? A rule works if it fires on a known event within a defined window. Everything else is an assumption. Most teams treat “deployed and enabled” as the working state: the rule exists in the SIEM, it passes validation at deploy time, the coverage heatmap stays green. Execution status and coverage status both measure presence, not function. A rule that executes successfully against an empty result set looks identical, from the platform’s perspective, to a rule watching a quiet network. The dashboard stays green either way. The honest evidence ladder has five tiers, weakest to strongest: Tier State What it proves What it does NOT prove 0 Asserted The rule exists Nothing about function 1 Lint-passed Parses correctly, required blocks present, fields exist in the target schema That it matches anything 2 Fixture-replayed Matches recorded known-bad events, rejects paired benign fixtures (offline) That it fires in the live pipeline 3 Emulation-validated Fires end to end against an emulated real procedure ( Atomic Red Team or MITRE Caldera ) in the deployed pipeline That the adversary’s real procedure emits this event in THIS environ
